visual.general_description: Three separate images: two 12-lead electrocardiogram tracings on pink gridded paper and one blue-tinted frontal chest radiograph with a printed R marker.
visual.detailed_description: Three separate image files are bound to this figure, numbered here in the order of the bound files, and no panel letters are printed on them. Image 1 is an ECG tracing on pale pink grid paper laid out in four rows: three rows of short lead segments in four columns and a full-width strip along the bottom. Tiny lead labels are printed beside the segments but are too small and blurred to read reliably. The complexes are widely spaced, about seven across the bottom strip; in the lower traces and the bottom strip each sharp deflection is followed by a rounded raised segment before the baseline returns, while the top-row traces show smaller deflections with flatter segments. Image 2 is a second ECG tracing on a stronger pink grid with the same four-row layout. Its complexes are more closely spaced, about fifteen across the bottom strip, and the third-column traces of the second and third rows show tall narrow deflections. Image 3 is a blue-tinted frontal chest radiograph with a white serif capital R at the upper left, showing both lung fields with ribs and clavicles, a pale central mediastinal and cardiac opacity that widens toward the lower part of the image, and the diaphragm domes along the bottom. A hazy grey-white area lies above the diaphragm dome on the side of the R marker, while the opposite lower lung field is darker up to its dome. No gastric air bubble can be identified below either dome at this resolution. No names, dates, calibration marks or numeric values are readable on any of the three images.

visual.general_description: Four grayscale coronary angiographic frames, each with an ECG trace along the bottom edge; the fourth frame carries two black arrows.
visual.detailed_description: Four separate grayscale angiographic frames are bound to this figure, numbered here in the order of the bound files, and none prints a panel letter, projection label or other text. Image 1 shows a branching contrast-filled vessel tree that fans across the left and centre from a junction at the upper right, a thin straight dark line (catheter-like) running down the right side, and a white ECG trace of about five complexes along the lower left edge. Image 2 shows a thick contrast-filled tubular vessel running from a dense dark tip near the left edge toward the centre, where thick curved or looping vessels and a round dark oval shape are seen, thin curved lines running along the left margin, from the top toward the centre and down the right side, and a white ECG trace along the bottom. Image 3 shows a long arching vessel along the left from the upper centre down to the lower left, a thick vessel at the upper centre running to the upper right and ending in a dark rounded end, a vessel tree descending through the centre, two long thin straight lines crossing the frame diagonally, and a white ECG trace at the lower left. Image 4 shows a thick C-shaped contrast-filled vessel in the centre right with a second parallel vessel below it and finer vessels at the left, two thin near-vertical lines at the right, an outlined open black arrow at the upper right pointing down and to the left toward the outer edge of the vessel, a solid black arrow at the lower centre pointing up and to the left toward the lower vessel segment, and a white ECG trace at the lower left. The caption and text do not say what the arrows mark.

evidence.quote: Modifi cations were made for image acquisition during coronary angiography (Figure 2).

The morphological LCA was engaged in the usual AP projection, but the morphological RCA was engaged in RAO projection (instead of LAO). For the LCA, LAO Caudal view became the ‘spider’ view; RAO Caudal became the LAO Caudal view and RAO Cranial became the LAO Cranial View. For the RCA, LAO became the RAO view and LAO became the RAO view.
